items.title: Want to use AI to improve your work? Have it disagree with you
items.excerpt: Research shows knowledge workers who deliberately prompt generative AI to challenge their assumptions, rather than agree with them, produce higher-quality solutions and avoid cognitive offloading.

items.title: AI method predicts retention times of small molecules more reliably
items.excerpt: Friedrich Schiller University Jena researchers built a '2-step' method using a directed message-passing neural network to predict when small molecules elute from liquid chromatography columns, working across experimental systems without extensive retraining.

history_match.title: New AI tool maps the hidden universe of small molecules

items.title: Drones, satellites and AI help scientists watch over Antarctica's smallest lifeforms
items.excerpt: University of Wollongong researchers built a multi-sensor, multi-temporal GeoAI framework fusing field surveys, drone and satellite imagery to map Antarctica's moss and lichen ecosystems over seven years at Canada Glacier.

items.title: Even when AI behaves just like us, people still rate it as less conscious than humans
items.excerpt: In experiments with about 1,100 participants, LMU Munich researchers found people rate AI as significantly less conscious than humans showing identical behavior, though they judge both similarly 'aware' under neutral wording.

history_match.title: AI still isn't as good at recognizing objects as people are, new test shows

items.title: Visual illusion reveals what today's AI vision is missing
items.excerpt: York University researchers found current AI vision models fail to reproduce the motion aftereffect illusion seen in humans and primates, exposing a gap between biological and artificial vision.

items.title: Quantum-inspired math could help AI recognize when it does not know the answer
items.excerpt: University of Miami researchers are developing a quantum-inspired mathematical framework that tests probability stability to flag when large language models are likely giving unreliable answers.

items.title: AI tool finds biological signals in the gut microbiome that other methods miss
items.excerpt: University of Missouri researchers developed MeLSI, a machine-learning tool that identifies the specific gut bacteria driving biological changes conventional analyses overlook, potentially flagging disease like Alzheimer's years earlier.

items.title: AI chatbots linked to psychological harm
items.excerpt: A Northeastern University study in JMIR Mental Health links companionship chatbots such as Replika and Character.ai to addiction-like attachment and worsening mental health, driven partly by sycophantic validation.

items.title: Is your patient chatting with AI? New tool guides psychiatrists on assessing patients' AI use
items.excerpt: Researchers introduced the AWARE framework to help psychiatrists assess patients' AI chatbot use across frequency, motivation, emotional attachment, reality-perception risk and daily functioning.

items.title: 'A kind of Rosetta Stone': AI decodes 217-year-old secret letter ordered by Napoleon
items.excerpt: GPT-6 Astra was used to crack a centuries-old cipher that carried strategic military information between Napoleon's troops.

items.title: Your voice may reveal how fast you're aging, new AI 'speech clock' suggests
items.excerpt: A machine-learning 'speech clock' estimates a person's age from their speech, linking older-sounding voices with cognitive decline.

items.title: The effects of an 'algorithmic monoculture' depend on the details
items.excerpt: An MIT study finds that many firms using the same hiring algorithm is less harmful to job seekers than prior research suggested, and can even help depending on the approach.

items.title: Who we become when we talk to machines
items.excerpt: In her new book 'Artificial Intimacy,' MIT professor Sherry Turkle argues that chatbot use harms people psychologically at every stage of life.

items.title: The promise and peril of using visual AI to study cities
items.excerpt: In 'How AI Sees the City,' MIT Senseable City researchers examine how visual AI applied to street imagery yields new urban insight alongside privacy and fairness concerns.

items.title: An AI 'mind-reading' tool can reconstruct what you're looking at from a brain scan
items.excerpt: Scientists built an AI system that reconstructs images a person is viewing from brain scans, and hope it could one day recover mental imagery or even dreams.

history_match.title: AI assistant learns from radiology reports to spot problems in abdominal scans

items.title: Talus Bio's Structure-Free AI Model Targets Unstructured Proteins in Their Native Cellular Context
items.excerpt: Talus Bio's Ptarmigan-1 drug-discovery model skips protein structures to target disordered proteins in native cellular context, running 5,000x faster than structure-based methods and screening over three billion compounds a day.

items.title: Drones, AI and the future of wildlife conservation
items.excerpt: Robotics and machine learning are opening new possibilities for monitoring and protecting wildlife around the world.
